findings.recommendation: Reduce parameter count by grouping related inputs into a value object.

remediation_details.remediation: Create a value object to hold the six parameters and pass it to the method
remediation_details.best_practice_explanation: Reducing the number of parameters in a method makes the code easier to read and understand. By grouping related inputs into a value object, we can improve code maintainability and reduce the likelihood of errors caused by incorrect parameter ordering.

findings.recommendation: Split the method into smaller helpers with a single responsibility.

remediation_details.remediation: Extract a helper method to sum values greater than 10
remediation_details.best_practice_explanation: Splitting the long method into smaller helpers improves readability and maintainability. The single responsibility principle is applied by creating a separate method for summing values greater than 10, making the code easier to understand and test.

findings.recommendation: Flatten the control flow using guard clauses or extracted methods.

remediation_details.remediation: Extract methods for each condition or use guard clauses to reduce nesting
remediation_details.best_practice_explanation: Reducing deep nesting improves code readability and maintainability. By extracting a method for the conditional addition, we simplify the main method and make it easier to understand and modify.

findings.recommendation: Split the class into smaller cohesive components.

remediation_details.remediation: Split the class into smaller classes, each with its own responsibility
remediation_details.best_practice_explanation: Splitting the class into smaller components improves maintainability, readability, and reusability. Each class should have a single responsibility, making it easier to modify and extend without affecting other parts of the codebase.

remediation_details.remediation: Group parameters into a single object
remediation_details.corrected_code_example: public class GoodCode { public int processOrder(Order order) { int result = 0; if (order.getA() > 10) { result += order.getA(); if (order.getB() > 10) { result += order.getB(); if (order.getC() > 10) { result += order.getC(); if (order.getD() > 10) { result += order.getD(); if (order.getE() > 10) { result += order.getE(); if (order.getF() > 10) { result += order.getF(); } } } } } } return result; } } class Order { private int a, b, c, d, e, f; public Order(int a, int b, int c, int d, int e, int f) { this.a = a; this.b = b; this.c = c; this.d = d; this.e = e; this.f = f; } public int getA() { return a; } public int getB() { return b; } public int getC() { return c; } public int getD() { return d; } public int getE() { return e; } public int getF() { return f; } }
remediation_details.best_practice_explanation: Grouping related parameters into a single object improves code readability and maintainability, reducing the likelihood of errors when calling methods with many parameters.

remediation_details.remediation: Extract a helper method to reduce nesting
remediation_details.best_practice_explanation: Reducing deep nesting improves code readability and maintainability by breaking down complex logic into smaller, more manageable pieces.

remediation_details.remediation: Split the class into OrderProcessor and Helper classes
remediation_details.best_practice_explanation: Splitting the class into smaller classes improves maintainability, readability, and follows the Single Responsibility Principle (SRP), which states that a class should have only one reason to change.
